items.text: Known caveats of the JSONStorage read-cache change (Nov 2026): read() now returns the same shared dict on each call (like CachingMiddleware), so a raising update callback could leave cached data half-modified; a deepcopy would fix it but lose most of the speedup, so it was not done. Table._query_cache is cleared only by this process's own writes, so a repeated identical search() returns stale results after importer writes; this predates the change and is left open (possible fixes: let Table ask storage whether the file changed, or disable the query cache). Files replaced by rename are also not detected as changed, since the open handle stays on the old file. Open follow-up: the user was asked whether to fix query-cache staleness next and had not answered.

JSONStorage.read() in tinydb/storages.py now has a read cache (implemented Nov 2026, uncommitted on branch perf/read-cache): each read() does os.fstat on the open handle and compares (mtime_ns, size, inode) with the signature of the last parse, returning the cached object on a match and re-parsing otherwise so importer-process writes are seen. A file modified within the last 2 seconds is never cached, because coarse timestamps could hide a same-size rewrite; write() clears the cache. All 229 tests pass, including a new external-write test. Benchmark (scripts/bench_read.py, 40 MB file): ~35 ms cached search versus ~350 ms raw json.load.

items.text: Design decision on caching JSONStorage reads (Nov 2026): initially undecided (the user deferred it to think about it; candidates were an instance-level cache invalidated on own write(), a content fingerprint, an explicit version marker, or opt-in middleware like CachingMiddleware; orjson was also discussed). Constraint: db files live on an NFS share with 1-second mtime resolution, and a previous mtime-based cache was removed last year because the importer wrote within the same second and stale data was served. Later the same day, a cache keyed on the os.fstat signature (mtime_ns, size, inode) was implemented on branch perf/read-cache, with files modified in the last 2 seconds never cached to guard against coarse timestamps; it is uncommitted. Suggested test: write twice within one second with different content.

items.text: Read-path performance profile of TinyDB (benchmarked Nov 2026 with scripts/bench_read.py, committed as 6b78af5 on branch perf/read-cache as part of the perf initiative; options --size-mb, --repeat, --keep). The script generates a ~40MB db and times raw json.load, db.all(), uncached and cached db.search(), plus a cProfile breakdown of one uncached search. On a 42.6 MB file with 115k docs: raw json.load ~340 ms, db.all() ~690 ms (about twice the parse because of Document/doc-ID wrapping), selective uncached db.search() ~410 ms, repeated identical search 0.1 ms. JSON parsing is ~85% of a selective search because JSONStorage.read() runs json.load on the whole file on every uncached read (tinydb/storages.py:140). Table.search() caches per query and writes clear the cache. No library code was changed by the benchmark.

items.text: Early v4 release history: v4.0.0 released 2020-05-02 with changelog, updated docs, upgrade notes and a Read the Docs configuration; v4.1.0 on 2020-05-07 (JSONStorage `access_mode` flag #297, noop/empty query operation #313, fix for next document ID calculation on an existing table #314); v4.1.1 on 2020-05-08; v4.2.0 on 2020-10-03.

Table API refactored for v4 (Jan 2020): next ID stored instead of last ID, `process_docs` removed, `Table.contains` accepts only a single doc ID (list semantics were ambiguous), `len(table)` faster, default cache capacity and default table name configurable. Goal: simplify the API and make method behavior clear. Later v4 additions: custom doc_ids on insertion (#303, June 2020) and docs on query cache caveats (#320): unlimited size/memory use and possibly stale results.

Table API enhancements (2020-2022): Table.get by doc_id made O(1) (#460), insert_multiple accepts Document instances, upsert() handles doc_id (#395), update_multiple added, and Table.delete() prefers doc_ids over cond (#424), aiming for consistent doc_id handling and performance.

Sept 2026 cache/ID correctness fixes: CachingMiddleware rejects reads/writes after close (#634); insert_multiple no longer reuses IDs in mixed batches, with _next_id typed Optional[int] (#633); LRUCache no longer treats stored None values as missing, using a sentinel default (#635). Earlier LRUCache fixes (v4.8.2) handled falsy values and updating existing keys.

Custom doc_ids during insertion were implemented in Table (#303); docs were added about the query cache having unlimited size/memory use and possibly stale results (#320). v4.2.0 was released on 2020-10-03. | When: 2020-06-06 to 2020-10-03 | Involving: Markus Siemens | Document query cache caveats

items.text: Internal refactor in October 2018 (commit e23b831, Claus Aichinger): type checks changed from isinstance-dict to isinstance-Mapping, allowing generic mapping types rather than only dict.

Table.update and Table.remove skip missing doc_ids instead of raising KeyError (May 2026), filtering IDs against the live table inside the updater before any side effects. This makes get/update/remove consistent and the operation atomic (previously mixed existing/missing IDs left documents half-updated in memory because docs are shared by reference), and lets upsert drop its KeyError branch.

items.text: TinyDB underwent a major architecture refactor for v4.0 (commit 50d0cd8, 'refactor: use new architecture', rationale in #284, closing #250 and #103), in November 2019 by Markus Siemens. It was accompanied by removal of Python 2 support, the deprecated ujson support and the deprecated element ID API. As part of the 'Extension Mechanisms' in #284, subclassing helpers were added ('feature: add subclassing helpers') to make TinyDB easier to extend, and type annotations were added across the code (2019-11-02 to 2019-11-15).
A warning about data loss/corruption risks with certain JSONStorage access_mode options was added in code and docs in February 2023 (commits 505d782, d0416e9), closing #506.

Docs and type hints were aligned with runtime behavior in October 2026 (issue #630): Query.test typed Callable[..., bool], operations.add accepts str, usage.rst update_multiple example fixed, Table.get docstring corrected, Query.search flags documented as going to re.search, and the invented _id field removed from the package docstring.

items.text: YAML support testing: commits 'Ensure YAML tests are run' and 'Pyyaml in setup.py' added PyYAML as a dependency in setup.py so YAML tests can run.

Table.get gained a doc_ids parameter (May-June 2023, commit 6f03ec6 by Mohammad Mohtashim) allowing multiple documents to be fetched by ID in one call; Markus Siemens later documented Table.get(doc_ids=[...]) (b8ffbfe). References #504, closes #486.

October 2026 query/table correctness fixes in TinyDB: Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes as sequences (is_sequence uses collections.abc.Sequence excluding str/bytes/bytearray) (#641); regex flags are now part of the matches/search query hash so differing flags don't share a query-cache entry (#640); persist_empty=True no longer wipes existing table data on reopen (#642).

TinyDB underwent a major architecture refactor for v4.0 (commit 50d0cd8, 'refactor: use new architecture'), with rationale documented in #284; it closed #250 and #103. It was accompanied by removal of Python 2 support, the deprecated `ujson` support and the deprecated element ID API. | When: 2019-11-02 | Involving: Markus Siemens | Modernize the codebase and simplify the architecture for v4.0 (#284)
